raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-symm-mem`, `ncclCommWindowRegister` is called from the forward
path whenever the symmetric-memory pool grows a new segment. That call blocks
in NCCL's Unix-domain-socket fd-exchange rendezvous, which has no timeout of
its own. When the rendezvous wedges, every rank in the group parks in `recvmsg`
and nothing is ever printed: the engine stays up, `/health` keeps returning
200, and no batch makes progress (#36943).

We hit exactly this on a single-node TP8/EP8 Kimi-K3 deployment with MegaMoE:
the engine hung on the first warmup prefill and the server log contained no
error line at all — the only way to tell it apart from an idle engine was to
notice that the log had stopped advancing. Roughly one cold-compile-cache start
in five hung this way.

The scheduler watchdog does eventually notice and dumps, but it cannot say
*what* was in flight, and it waits its full `--watchdog-timeout` (300 s by
default) before it does.

## Modifications

- The registration runs on a worker thread bounded by
  `SGLANG_SYMM_MEM_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_S` (default 120 s), so a wedge is
  reported sooner than the watchdog would report it.
- On timeout the registration is named in the log, `pyspy_dump_schedulers()` and
  `faulthandler.dump_traceback()` capture the native and Python stacks, and the
  parent is sent `SIGQUIT` — the same exit path the scheduler and the watchdog
  use, so the normal crash handling runs. The process does not continue: the
  wedged thread still holds the C++ segment mutex, so it could never register
  again.
- `describe_registration_in_progress()` publishes what is in flight, and the
  scheduler watchdog's `dump_info()` includes it, so a stall there reads as
  "symmetric-memory registration in progress: comm=… group=…" instead of a bare
  watchdog timeout.

This does **not** remove the underlying deadlock; it makes it named, fast and
diagnosable. The root cause is tracked in #36943.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - no change to numerics.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A - the registration call itself is unchanged. The added work is one thread
start plus one join per registration round, and a round only happens when the
symmetric-memory pool grows a segment.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with
      pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit
      tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
      `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_pynccl_allocator_registration_timeout.py`
      covers the bound, the exception passthrough, the timeout path and the
      published state; 5 tests pass on the 0.5.21 image.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write
      documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
      Not applicable: the new env var is a diagnostic bound, not a user-facing
      feature, and no behaviour changes when the registration succeeds.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the
      accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)
      and [Benchmark the
      speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
      N/A, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style
      [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 import ctypes
+import faulthandler
 import logging
 import os
+import signal
 import tempfile
+import threading
 import traceback
 from contextlib import nullcontext
+from typing import Optional
 
+import psutil
 import torch
 
 # The private _cuda_* pool APIs are absent before torch 2.8; the call sites below
@@ -234,6 +239,52 @@ def get_nccl_mem_pool() -> torch.cuda.MemPool:
     return _mem_pool
 
 
+# NCCL's window registration blocks in a Unix-domain-socket fd-exchange
+# rendezvous that has no timeout of its own. When that rendezvous loses a
+# message, every rank in the group sits in recvmsg with no error and no log
+# line: the engine stays up, `/health` keeps returning 200, and no batch can
+# make progress. Bound the wait (SGLANG_SYMM_MEM_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_S) so a
+# wedge is reported instead of hidden, and keep the in-progress state readable
+# so the scheduler watchdog can name it rather than reporting a bare stall.
+
+_registration_in_progress: Optional[str] = None
+
+
+def describe_registration_in_progress() -> Optional[str]:
+    """What the symmetric-memory registration is doing, or ``None`` if idle.
+
+    The scheduler watchdog reads this for its dump, so a stall inside the
+    registration is named instead of showing up as a generic watchdog timeout.
+    """
+    return _registration_in_progress
+
+
+def _run_with_timeout(fn, timeout_s: float):
+    """Run ``fn()`` on a worker thread and return its result.
+
+    Raises ``TimeoutError`` if it has not returned within ``timeout_s``; any
+    other exception raised by ``fn`` is re-raised. The worker is a daemon, so a
+    call that never returns cannot keep the process alive by itself.
+    """
+
+    outcome: dict = {}
+
+    def _target():
+        try:
+            outcome["result"] = fn()
+        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised by the caller
+            outcome["exc"] = exc
+
+    worker = threading.Thread(target=_target, name="symm-mem-register", daemon=True)
+    worker.start()
+    worker.join(timeout_s)
+    if worker.is_alive():
+        raise TimeoutError(f"did not return within {timeout_s:.0f}s")
+    if "exc" in outcome:
+        raise outcome["exc"]
+    return outcome["result"]
+
+
 class SymmetricMemoryContext:
     """
     Context manager for using symmetric memory with pynccl.
@@ -317,15 +368,64 @@ def _register_segments_for_comm(self):
         1. Tracking which segments have been registered with each comm
         2. Only registering new segments (avoiding re-registration)
         3. Thread-safe access to the segment registry
+
+        The call is bounded: see the module comment above.
         """
 
+        global _registration_in_progress
+
+        group = self.group_coordinator.unique_name
+        timeout_s = envs.SGLANG_SYMM_MEM_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_S.get()
+
         # Call C++ API to register all segments with this comm
         # C++ layer tracks per-comm registration state internally
-        result = _register_func(self._comm_ptr)
+        _registration_in_progress = f"comm={self._comm_ptr} group={group}"
+        logger.debug("Registering symmetric-memory segments with %s", group)
+        try:
+            result = _run_with_timeout(
+                lambda: _register_func(self._comm_ptr),
+                timeout_s,
+            )
+        except TimeoutError:
+            self._report_registration_timeout(group, timeout_s)
+            raise  # unreachable: the report exits the process
+        finally:
+            _registration_in_progress = None
         assert result == 0, (
             f"nccl_allocator_register_segments_with_comm failed with return code: {result}"
         )
 
+    def _report_registration_timeout(self, group: str, timeout_s: float) -> None:
+        """Give up loudly: the group is wedged and no batch can make progress.
+
+        NCCL's registration has no timeout of its own, so without this the
+        engine would sit here indefinitely with `/health` still answering 200.
+        Take the same exit path as any other scheduler failure: dump what a
+        maintainer needs, then SIGQUIT the parent so the normal crash handling
+        runs, and stop this process because the wedged thread still holds the
+        C++ segment mutex -- it could never register again.
+        """
+        logger.error(
+            "Symmetric-memory registration for comm %s (group %s) did not return "
+            "within %.0f s. Every rank in the group is wedged in NCCL's "
+            "fd-exchange rendezvous: the engine is up and /health answers 200, "
+            "but no batch can make progress. Dumping stacks and aborting.",
+            self._comm_ptr,
+            group,
+            timeout_s,
+        )
+        try:
+            from sglang.srt.utils.cudacore_pyspy_dump_utils import (
+                pyspy_dump_schedulers,
+            )
+
+            pyspy_dump_schedulers()
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Failed to dump scheduler stacks")
+        faulthandler.dump_traceback()
+        psutil.Process().parent().send_signal(signal.SIGQUIT)
+        os._exit(1)
+

     disabled = (

@@ -1881,6 +1881,10 @@ class Envs:

     SGLANG_SYMM_MEM_PREALLOC_GB_SIZE = EnvInt(-1)
     SGLANG_DEBUG_SYMM_MEM = EnvBool(False)
+    # NCCL's window registration has no timeout of its own, so a lost message in
+    # its fd-exchange rendezvous hangs every rank silently. Give up after this
+    # many seconds and report instead.
+    SGLANG_SYMM_MEM_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_S = EnvFloat(120.0)
 
     # Qwen3.5 and GDN
     SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_DECODE_FUSED_PROJ_CONV = EnvBool(True)

@@ -500,11 +500,22 @@ def dump_info() -> str:
         _, messages = scheduler.invariant_checker._check_all_pools(
             scheduler.pool_stats_observer.get_pool_stats(),
         )
-        return (
-            f"{scheduler.cur_batch_for_debug.batch_size()=}\n"
-            f"{scheduler.cur_batch_for_debug.reqs=}\n" + "\n".join(messages)
+        parts = [
+            f"{scheduler.cur_batch_for_debug.batch_size()=}",
+            f"{scheduler.cur_batch_for_debug.reqs=}",
+        ]
+        # Name the stall when it is the symmetric-memory registration, whose
+        # collective has no timeout of its own and would otherwise be reported
+        # as a generic watchdog timeout.
+        from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.pynccl_allocator import (
+            describe_registration_in_progress,
         )
 
+        if (registration := describe_registration_in_progress()) is not None:
+            parts.append(f"symmetric-memory registration in progress: {registration}")
+        parts.extend(messages)
+        return "\n".join(parts)
+
     return WatchdogRaw(
         debug_name="Scheduler",
         get_counter=lambda: scheduler.forward_ct,

@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+"""Bounding the symmetric-memory window registration.
+
+NCCL's window registration blocks in a Unix-domain-socket fd-exchange
+rendezvous that has no timeout of its own. When that rendezvous wedges, every
+rank in the group sits in recvmsg with no error and no log line, `/health`
+keeps answering 200, and the engine silently serves nothing
+(sgl-project/sglang#36943). ``_run_with_timeout`` is what turns that into a
+reported failure, and ``describe_registration_in_progress`` is what lets the
+scheduler watchdog name the stall.
+"""
+
+import time
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators import pynccl_allocator
+from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.pynccl_allocator import (
+    _run_with_timeout,
+    describe_registration_in_progress,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestRunWithTimeout(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_returns_result(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_run_with_timeout(lambda: 7, timeout_s=5.0), 7)
+
+    def test_propagates_exception(self):
+        def boom():
+            raise RuntimeError("registration failed")
+
+        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            _run_with_timeout(boom, timeout_s=5.0)
+
+    def test_times_out_instead_of_hanging(self):
+        def never_returns():
+            time.sleep(30)
+
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        with self.assertRaises(TimeoutError):
+            _run_with_timeout(never_returns, timeout_s=0.2)
+        # The bound decided when to give up, not the call.
+        self.assertLess(time.monotonic() - started, 5.0)
+
+
+class TestDescribeRegistrationInProgress(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_idle_by_default(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(describe_registration_in_progress())
+
+    def test_reports_what_is_in_flight(self):
+        pynccl_allocator._registration_in_progress = "comm=1 group=tp"
+        try:
+            self.assertEqual(
+                describe_registration_in_progress(), "comm=1 group=tp"
+            )
+        finally:
+            pynccl_allocator._registration_in_progress = None
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
